item.title: Stripe Tells You the Money Arrived. On-Chain, Nobody Does — Building a USDC Verification Engine
item.guid: title:stripe tells you the money arrived on chain nobody does building a usdc verification engine
item.description: Short answer: When a buyer pays by card, Stripe's webhook says "paid". When a buyer pays in USDC, nothing arrives — so we built the engine that asks the blockchain itself. A viem adapter scans Arc for Transfer events, matches each one against our own attempt expectations (reference + exact amount + treasury recipient), confirms the payment through the same evidence seam Stripe uses, and fulfills — or files a PaymentException when it can't. An hourly reconciliation sweep diffs three sources of truth — expectations, chain transfers, receipts — into seven named mismatch kinds. Then we ran an adversarial audit on all of it: 2 Critical + 9 High, every finding re-verified against the source, all fixed with regression tests. Ask the source, not the messenger.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: How I'm thinking about different types of automated alignment
item.guid: title:how i m thinking about different types of automated alignment
item.description: I used to think of "automating alignment" as a natural category. But when I tried to think through the strategic implications, I realised that it depends a lot on the type of work. I'm now thinking of it in three buckets: Empirical alignment research : design and execution of alignment-relevant experiments (for a given notion of what we’re aiming for) Conceptual alignment research: theoretical or judgement-driven work to improve our understanding of what we’re aiming for and how to achieve it (including how to measure it) Direct alignment work : making particular AI systems more aligned (including via inputs such as training data) In the rest of this post I'll walk through my current takes on these in terms what’s needed for automation, how good or bad they look, what our priorities might be (to the extent we're interested in automating alignment [1] ), etc. Automating empirical alignment research This is the most obvious fit for the AI capabilities we’re getting at the moment. You want to know more about the relationship between some alignment-relevant variables? Great, an AI agent can design and run that experiment for you.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.
